text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Bank ABN AMRO sells its five percent stake in
retailer Macintosh to household goods and toys chain
store Blokker. (p1)
- Financial services group Price Waterhouse plans to conquer
Dutch market for outsourcing of administrative services. (p1)
- Rabobank [RABN.CN] is to start trials with a "cyber
shopping centre" on the Internet. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Junior Finance Minister plans to present a plan for
heavier taxation of share option schemes for senior managers.
- Charter flight company Martinair to seek compensation from
Schiphol Airport following ban on night flights. (p2)
- Dutch price inflation of 2.3 pct yr/yr now running faster
than in neighbouring countries. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Employers association VNO-NCW and labour union FNV have
been awarded prestigious German Carl Bertelsmann award for their
role in strengthening the Dutch economy. (p1)
- Philips Electronics decides not to take action
against employees of its unit Pie Medical unit who are being
investigated in alleged case of insider share trading. (p1)
- Tropical temperatures force up potato prices on Amsterdam
agricultural commodities exchange. (p22)
TROUW
- KLM could face fine of up to one billion guilders
as European Commission is convinced the airline is trying to
force low-price competitor EasyJet out of business. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Chief executive of paper and packaging KNP BT's
U.S. unit BT Office Products leaves the company. (p10)
-- Amsterdam newsdesk +31 20 504 5000
